messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired -> P1 reserved_capacity_exhaustion on dedicated-harborfin-01.
incident-bot: alert_id=PD-98321, runbook=https://runbooks.internal/redwood/reserved-capacity-exhaustion, dashboard=https://grafana.redwood/d/harborfin/reserved-capacity

maya: acked. I'm on it. grabbing dashboards now.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by maya. Escalation timeout set to 10m.

liam: seeing a clear 5x jump in 95p latency for generation requests starting ~10:23 UTC, sustained QPS increase from 120 -> 340. embeddings also 503ing intermittently. link: https://grafana.redwood/d/harborfin/latency-overview

maya: confirmed 503s and queued requests piling on dedicated-harborfin-01 pool. KV-cache hit-rate dropped (cache evictions spiked). suspect burst capacity exhausted.

maya: quick checklist I'm running:
- check pool headroom
- attempt soft-burst enable if policy allows
- fall back routing to compatible model variant if latency unacceptable

tess: running headroom query now (internal CLI). paste output:
```
$ rcli reserved describe --tenant harborfin --pool dedicated-harborfin-01\pool_size: 12 GPUs\allocated: 12\headroom: 0\queued: 742\pending_evictions: 34\```

liam: that matches. autoscale attempted but throttled by reserved commit. burst capacity currently disabled for this tenant per contract.

sanjay: pinging HarborFin account ops to let them know we're investigating. they reported customer-facing errors ~10:26 UTC.

maya: mitigation plan (short):
1) temporarily open burst window for 15m (requires oncall approval) to drain queue.
2) enable model-variant-fallback on route to map to smaller-quantized model (latency up, quality slightly down).
3) if burst open not possible, start controlled drop: reject lowest-priority routes and route to hosted fallback region.

liam: +1 to opening burst. cost impact acknowledged. we need explicit ack to bypass contractual cap.

pagerduty-bot: Escalating to oncall-next (tess) due to ack timeout.

oncall-next: I'm seeing thread. if maya gives the go I'll approve burst override. how long to drain?

maya: estimated drain ~9-12m once burst opens. queue draining rate ~90r/s with burst vs 10r/s current.

sanjay: HarborFin ops says they can tolerate up to 10m of diminished quality if that prevents 503s. they're ok with fallback to the quantized variant.

maya: performing burst override now: `rcli reserved burst-enable --tenant harborfin --duration 900s --reason "P1 drain"`

incident-bot: Action logged by maya: burst-enable request submitted. request_id=REQ-7712.

tess: I can see pool draining. queued down from 742 -> 320 in 3m. KV-cache warming starting.

liam: adding a temporary route rule to prefer smaller-quant models for embedding routes:
```json
{"match": "tenant:harborfin", "route": "model:hf-mini-q4_8b", "priority": 10}
```
applied via `rcli routes apply --file tmp-route.json`

maya: applied fallback route. monitoring errors.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: burst-enable approved by oncall-next. escalation cleared.

sanjay: HarborFin acknowledges reduced errors on their side, reporting ~20% error rate -> now <1%. they want a post-incident summary when stable.

maya: metrics look good. 95p latency back to near-normal for gen and embeddings error rate trending to 0.

tess: follow-up tasks:
- create CR to enable scheduled burst policies for burst-tolerant tenants
- add a guardrail to auto-open burst for X minutes for P1 when headroom==0 and queued>500
- include this tenant's traffic pattern in optimize recommendations

liam: note: we should check why KV-cache eviction spiked. could be model change or memory pressure on node. I'll open an infra ticket.

maya: handoff: I'll remain on this thread for 10 more minutes then hand to oncall-next for watch.

oncall-next: taking watch. will escalate if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (soft): P1 -> mitigated. will remain open for postmortem.

sanjay: Thanks team. I'll coordinate customer comms and include the mitigation timeline.

maya: short timeline to include in postmortem:
- 10:23 UTC: spike begins
- 10:26 UTC: PagerDuty fired
- 10:31 UTC: burst override requested
- 10:34 UTC: burst active, queue draining
- 10:45 UTC: errors <1%, traffic stable

tess: logging actions to incident tracker: INC-2026. tagging infra and product.

liam: one-liner for PMs: Dedicated pool exhausted due to sudden traffic spike; burst policy manually enabled to drain queue; KV-cache eviction correlated; follow-ups: auto-burst guardrail + cache root cause.

maya: leaving thread now, thanks all :thumbsup:

oncall-next: acknowledged. closing watch in 30m unless new alerts.

incident-bot: thread archived for record.
